findings.quote: -        let written = "no flock at /tmp/x\n  to set up a flock there deliberately: mkdir -p /tmp/x";
findings.what: The old convention put the two-space indent inside the message. This commit only updates the test fixture, not the production messages, so any refusal still written as `\n  ...` will now print a four-space indent in table mode.

Only a truly empty line escapes the indent. A line holding only whitespace (e.g. from `"a\n \nb"` or an interpolated value) is still indented, so a paragraph break gains the trailing whitespace this function says it avoids, and `trim_end` only strips the end of the whole message.
